defects.rationale: The default list is created once and shared across calls, so tags accumulate across separate invocations.

issues.observation: The review reports exactly one finding (mutable_default at line 1). A single-finding review is the classic signature of stopping after the easiest issue; mutable-default arguments are rarely the only material defect in a snippet long enough to be submitted for review. No other candidate areas (input validation, error handling, resource lifetime, concurrency, injection surfaces) are addressed or explicitly ruled out.
issues.rubric_criterion: coverage — identifies distinct material defects visible in the supplied snippet, including interacting defects when present

issues.observation: Line 1 is cited as the location of a mutable default argument. For that to hold, line 1 must be the function signature line containing the `=[]` (or equivalent) default. If the snippet begins with imports, a decorator, or a docstring, the correct defect is attached to the wrong line, which costs the frozen category-and-line F1 directly.
issues.rubric_criterion: evidence_alignment — the cited line contains the operation responsible for the stated failure

issues.observation: The rationale states accumulation across invocations but does not tie it to the specific observable failure in this code (e.g., which caller-visible value is corrupted, or which returned structure grows unboundedly). It reads as the generic textbook description of the pattern rather than a trace through this snippet.
issues.rubric_criterion: concrete_defect / evidence_alignment — rationale must explain the concrete failure path, not name a generic risk

revision_instructions: Re-read the snippet line by line and confirm that line 1 is the exact line containing the mutable default parameter. If the default appears on a different line (e.g., a multi-line signature), update the line number to the line holding the `=[]`/`={}` token.

Make a second pass over the whole snippet looking for additional material defects in these categories: unvalidated or unsanitized input reaching a query/command/path, unchecked return values or swallowed exceptions, resources opened without guaranteed close, off-by-one or boundary errors in indexing/slicing, state mutated while iterating, and race or TOCTOU windows. Add each distinct one as its own finding.

Where two defects interact (for example, the shared mutable default being mutated by a code path that also lacks validation), add the interaction as a separate finding and state in the rationale how the two combine to worsen the failure.
Rewrite the existing rationale so it traces the concrete failure in this code: name the parameter, name the mutation site, and state what a second caller observes as a result.
Keep the existing mutable_default finding intact unless its line number is provably wrong; do not reword or recategorize it while adding new findings.
Stay within eight findings total, ensure no two findings share the same category and line, and keep every line number within the bounds of the supplied snippet.
